title: Press Regulating Act 1942
definition: The Press Regulating Act of 1942 was a wartime emergency measure promulgated by the British colonial government under the Defence of India Rules to suppress nationalist reporting during the Quit India Movement.
importanceInUpsc: It represents the peak of colonial censorship during the Second World War, illustrating the conflict between imperial security and the freedom of the press in the context of the Indian National Movement.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Press Regulating Act 1942.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Evolution of Press Laws in India
